How to protect yourself from scams. Scammers often pretend to be your bank. They may say your account has been locked or that there is unusual activity, and push you to act immediately. First National Bank will never ask you to buy gift cards, move money to a safe account, or share a one-time passcode. Warning signs of a scam: pressure to act right away, requests for remote access to your computer, and being told to keep it secret. If something feels wrong, hang up and call the number on the back of your card. Report fraud to our team at any branch.

Consumer advice: Gift card scams. Only scammers will tell you to buy a gift card, like a Google Play or Apple card, and send them the codes. Scammers may say they are from the IRS, tech support, or a family member in trouble, and that you must pay immediately. How to spot the scam: they say it is urgent, they tell you which gift card to buy, they ask you to read the numbers off the back, and they tell you not to tell the cashier. If you paid a scammer with a gift card, report it to the card company right away. Report a scam to the consumer protection agency.

TeamViewer Remote. Secure remote access and support for IT teams. Connect to devices across your company, support employees wherever they work, and manage unattended servers. Free for personal use. Download for Windows. Security: protect yourself from misuse. We will never ask you to install our software by cold call. Only grant remote access to people you know and trust. How to recognize a remote access scam.

IT Helpdesk knowledge base: Requesting remote support. If you have a problem with your work laptop, open a ticket in the staff portal. A named technician from the IT team will message you in the portal to arrange a remote session at a time that suits you. You will always see the technician's name and ticket number. Our team will never ask for your password. No action is needed until your ticket is assigned.

Tax scams and consumer alerts. The IRS does not initiate contact with taxpayers by email, text message or social media to request personal or financial information. The IRS will never ask for payment by gift card or wire transfer, and will never threaten arrest. Scammers often impersonate the IRS and demand that people pay immediately. How to recognize these scams and how to report phishing: forward suspicious messages to the reporting address listed on this page.

To see it, sign in to your personal account the way you usually do. This is an informational message and no action is required. Please do not reply to this email.

Medicare Open Enrollment runs from October 15 to December 7. During this time you can review your coverage and compare plans for next year. If you are happy with your current plan, you do not need to do anything. Medicare will never call you to sell you anything or ask for your Medicare number. Compare plans online or visit a local counselling office for free help.

Markets: Bitcoin slips as investors weigh interest rate outlook. Bitcoin fell 2.1 percent on Tuesday while Ethereum was little changed. Analysts said cryptocurrency prices remain volatile and investors can lose money. Regulators again warned consumers that no legitimate investment offers guaranteed returns, and urged people to report fraud. Elsewhere, shares in regional banks rose.

Help centre: How to send a wire transfer. You can send a domestic wire transfer from online banking or at any branch. You will need the recipient's name, bank routing number and account number. Wire transfers usually arrive the same business day and cannot be reversed once sent, so only send money to people you know and trust. Scammers often ask for wire transfers. Citywide Bank will never ask you to move money to protect it.

Blog: What to do about fake virus pop-ups. A sudden full-screen message saying your computer is infected and telling you to call a number is a tech support scam. Real security software never asks you to call a phone number. How to avoid it: do not call the number, do not let anyone connect to your computer, and close the browser. Scammers will try to keep you on the phone. How to protect yourself from these pop-ups and how to report a scam are explained below.
